notes: Lessons are not pages any more. A concept arrives one example at a time, in the middle of the screen, and the code runs itself in front of you: the bar slides down the lines as they execute, values physically fly out of the line that made them and land in the box that holds them, and each new line of output slides into the console. Nothing jumps.

Then it hands the same program back and asks you to run it. You click the lines in the order they actually execute, and each right click plays the same motion you just watched. Getting a line wrong shakes it and costs you nothing.

One thing on screen at a time. Everything that is not the line being run steps back so there is exactly one place to look, and the caption under it is a single short line with the variable and its value in their own colors.
A back button on every question that returns you to the lesson, and lessons can be watched again as many times as you like. Before this, a lesson was a gate you passed once and could never reopen.
Long lines of code wrap instead of sliding off the edge, so nothing ever disappears mid explanation.
Home offers one way forward instead of three. The session you are in the middle of is the thing it puts in front of you.
The scratchpad shows what Java actually said underneath the plain English version, with the line numbers corrected to match the code you typed rather than the file the app wraps around it.
Running code no longer freezes the window while it compiles, and two runs can no longer start at once, which is what made the app feel like it had hung when you pressed Run twice.
